source.title: Is Grokking a Loss of Normal Hyperbolicity of the Interpolation Manifold?

record.file_problem: Some equations and symbols are garbled by text extraction; the full paper is otherwise present.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports grokking on modular addition using train/test accuracy and tests a geometric explanation with a different diagnostic. It does not test how delay changes with training-set size.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own accuracy trajectory, Jacobian singular-value measurements, and parameter-norm observation. The cited results of other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study trains its own two-layer ReLU network on modular addition mod 11 and reports train and test accuracy curves showing delayed generalization (V1). It also reports the parameter norm through the transition (V5). Its main contribution is a Jacobian singular-value diagnostic, which no version names. The setup differs from the originals (MLP, squared loss, AdamW, large init), so this is a different method on the same question, not a replication.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. In a single gradual-transition AdamW setting, σmin+(J) does not collapse at the grokking transition; it is largest there, across five seeds and the six smallest singular values. The authors read this as preliminary evidence for smooth contraction (H0) over a bifurcation (H1), constraining rather than refuting it. They also note that ℓ2 norm does not contract under AdamW.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a small modular-addition task and train/test accuracy to observe grokking, but tests squared loss with AdamW, a two-layer width-96 ReLU network, and a Jacobian-singular-value diagnostic; it is not reported as a replication of the original recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports robustness across five initialization seeds. It does not sweep optimizer, initialization scale, or training-set size.

fits_no_version.finding: The smallest nonzero residual-Jacobian singular value is near zero only before memorization and peaks during the generalization transition. The six smallest singular values stay bounded away from zero, consistently across five seeds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking is not accompanied by a loss of normal hyperbolicity (a global collapse of the normal restoring rate) of the interpolation manifold; the transition looks like smooth drift.

record.peer_reviewed: Accepted for publication at SKILL 2026 (GI-Edition Lecture Notes in Informatics, Gesellschaft für Informatik e.V.)
record.problems: The study tests a single task, architecture, loss, and optimizer setting; the transition is described as moderately gradual; the trajectory is discrete rather than gradient flow; and the global singular-value diagnostic may miss a narrow test-relevant subspace. The authors also note that sharp-transition gradient-descent regimes are untested.

untested.parts: How the delay scales with training-set size; only one 70/30 split is used.
Circuit formation, memorization removal and circuit-based progress measures.
Non-algorithmic data, and switching grokking on or off by initialization scale. Large init is used, not swept.
Circuit efficiency, critical dataset size and ungrokking; norm contraction is examined only under AdamW.
No optimizer or numerical-precision controls; only AdamW is used.

missing.what: Across five seeds, the step at which test accuracy first exceeds 0.5 ranges from about 10,000 to 16,000, i.e. the grokking delay varies by seed.
Training hyperparameters that induce the plateau (Kaiming ×3.5 init, AdamW lr 3e-3, decoupled wd 2.0, full batch, 35,000 steps) are absent from row conditions.

record.verdict_notes: The large initialization was chosen to induce the plateau (following Omnigrok), but it is not varied, so V3 is untested. The final test accuracy of 0.86 is somewhat below 'near-perfect'; V1 support is kept with that caveat. Tranche T2 is kept. The originals (2201.02177, 2301.05217) are only cited.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses one 70%/30% train/test split and does not compare grokking delay across training-set sizes.
It does not measure formation of a generalizing circuit, removal of memorizing components, or continuous circuit-progress measures.
No non-algorithmic data, initialization-scale sweep, or lazy-to-rich transition comparison is tested.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is tested.
The study notes the parameter-norm trajectory but does not test whether a low-norm circuit is more efficient, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below such a size.
It does not identify or compare algorithms learned across runs.
It does not compare optimizers or control numerical choices to test whether the grokking delay is an artifact.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU network (five initialization seeds)
rows.operation_detail: Smallest residual-Jacobian singular value across five seeds
rows.value: In every seed, remains in the 0.18–0.23 range during its transition; no seed shows a dip

rows.note: Aggregate statement across five seeds; individual seed values are not reported in the text.
rows.check: The row could also record that per-seed transition timing varies (test accuracy first exceeds 0.5 between about steps 10,000 and 16,000). That fact bears on V1 and is not captured anywhere.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU network
rows.value: Stays near 10 and drifts slightly upward; does not decrease through the transition
rows.note: The authors treat this as a caveat about AdamW; they note its implicit bias may be governed by an ℓ∞-type rather than ℓ2 geometry.
rows.check: This is an ℓ2 norm under AdamW. The authors attribute the lack of contraction to AdamW's ℓ∞-type implicit bias, so it measures ℓ2 contraction specifically. The locator is 'Section 4, secondary observation'.

relationships.reason: Training accuracy reaches 1.0 by step ~4,000 while test accuracy stays at 0.0 until ~6,000, then rises to ~0.95 (settling ~0.86) (R1, R2).
